  {
    "operation": "etymology",
    "chain": "Fenway < Old English fenn (marsh, fen) + weg (way, path); Middle English fenwei",
    "reading": "A path through the marshland; a raised causeway crossing wet ground.",
    "languages": ["en", "ang"],
    "source": "Oxford English Dictionary, s.v. 'fen' and 'way'",
    "confidence": 0.9
  },
  {
    "operation": "phonetic_split",
    "chain": "Fen + way; fen (marsh) + way (route); also 'fen' as in 'fence' (enclosure) + 'way'",
    "reading": "The enclosed route; a guided passage within bounded limits.",
    "languages": ["en"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.6
  },
  {
    "operation": "cross_language_homophone",
    "chain": "Fen (fr: faim = hunger) + way (en); 'fenway' ~ 'faim voie' (hungry path) in French",
    "reading": "A road of hunger; a journey of desire or lack.",
    "languages": ["fr", "en"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.4
  },
  {
    "operation": "anagram",
    "chain": "Fenway → 'we fan y' → 'we fan' (we winnow) + 'y' (why); also 'wayfen' (way + fen)",
    "reading": "We winnow the why; a sifting of purpose along the path.",
    "languages": ["en"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.3
  },
  {
    "operation": "notariqon",
    "chain": "F-E-N-W-A-Y: Fons, Egressus, Numen, Via, Aether, Yggdrasil (Latin/Greek/Norse roots)",
    "reading": "Source, exit, divine will, road, sky, world-tree — a cosmic itinerary.",
    "languages": ["la", "grc", "non"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.2
  },
  {
    "operation": "letter_symbol",
    "chain": "F (fire, 6th letter) + E (earth, 5th) + N (water, 14th) + W (wind, 23rd) + A (air, 1st) + Y (spirit, 25th)",
    "reading": "The six elements in sequence: fire, earth, water, wind, air, spirit — a alchemical path.",
    "languages": ["en"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.5
  },
  {
    "operation": "numerical",
    "chain": "F=6, E=5, N=14, W=23, A=1, Y=25 → sum = 74; 74 = 7+4 = 11; 11 = master number",
    "reading": "The sum 74 reduces to 11 — a master number of illumination and revelation.",
    "languages": ["en"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.4
  },
  {
    "operation": "phonetic_split",
    "chain": "Fen + way; 'fen' (Dutch: ven = pool, bog) + 'way' (Old Norse: vegr = road)",
    "reading": "A bog-road; a track laid over unstable ground, needing faith to cross.",
    "languages": ["nl", "non", "en"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.5
  },
  {
    "operation": "cross_language_homophone",
    "chain": "Fenway ~ 'fin voie' (French: end of road) — 'fin' (end) + 'voie' (way)",
    "reading": "The end of the way; a terminal path, a conclusion of travel.",
    "languages": ["fr", "en"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.5
  },
  {
    "operation": "etymology",
    "chain": "Fenway < Old English fenn + weg; also 'fen' from Proto-Germanic *fanjam (marsh)",
    "reading": "A marsh-path; historically a route through wetlands, often used for grazing or trade.",
    "languages": ["en", "gem"],
    "source": "Klein's Comprehensive Etymological Dictionary of the English Language",
    "confidence": 0.85
  }
]
